properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 948466
Incident Time: 2010-07-16 19:45:00
Nearest City: Valdez, AK
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: GASOLINE: AUTOMOTIVE (UNLEADED)
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: ABR, INC.- ENV. RESEARCH AND SERVICES
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 3.28 feet by 3.28 feet (area 10.76 sq. ft.)
Reported Spill Volume: 0.06 gallons
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
ON FRIDAY, JULY 16, 2010 AT APPROXIMATELY 14:45 LOCAL TIME, A VERY SMALL FUEL SPILL OCCURRED IN ALLISON LAKE, NEAR VALDEZ, ALASKA. I WAS PERFORMING BIOLOGICAL SERVICES AIMED AT DETERMINING THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF FISH IN A MOUNTAIN LAKE AS PART OF THE FERC PROCESS FOR A PROPOSED HYDROELECTRIC FACILITY. THE WORK REQUIRED ME TO KEEP AN INFLATABLE BOAT ON SITE WITH A SMALL 4-STROKE MOTOR. GEAR AND PEOPLE WERE TRANSFERRED TO THE SITE BY HELICOPTER. DUE TO WEATHER ISSUES ON 14 JULY WE WERE KEPT FROM RETRIEVING OUR GEAR UNTIL THE AFTERNOON OF 16 JULY. WHEN I ARRIVED AT THE SITE AFTER A NEARLY 2 DAY ABSENCE I DISCOVERED THAT A BEAR (LIKELY A BLACK BEAR) HAD STREWN MY SAMPLING GEAR AND CONTAINERS ABOUT THE HILLSIDE. FURTHERMORE, THE BEAR PUNCTURED MY INFLATABLE BOAT, PARTIALLY DEFLATING THE SIDES BEFORE IT DRAG THE BOAT HALF ON SHORE, HALF OFF SHORE. THE BEAR ALSO PUNCTURED THE 3 GALLON FUEL TANK WHICH HAD CONTAINED ~1.5 GALLONS OF FUEL. THE FUEL LEAKED INTO THE BOAT AND WAS CONTAINED. HOWEVER, WHEN I WENT TO PULL THE BOAT FULLY ONSHORE, A VERY SMALL AMOUNT OF WATER/FUEL MIXTURE OVERFLOWED INTO THE LAKE IN THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF LAKE. I ESTIMATE THE AMOUNT TO BE LESS THAN 1 OZ. AND THAT THE SHEEN COVERED LESS THAN 1 SQ. METER SURFACE AREA. I QUICKLY ALTERED MY METHOD OF RETRIEVAL TO KEEP FROM SPILLING MORE FUEL IN THE WATER. WIND DISPERSED THE SHEEN WITHIN 10 MINUTES. I ESTIMATE THAT AN ADDITIONAL 1 FLUID CUP OF WATER/FUEL MIXTURE WAS LEAKED ONTO THE SHORE APPROXIMATELY 10 METERS FROM THE LAKE. THE BULK OF THE REMAINING FUEL APPEARS TO HAVE EVAPORATED OFF WITH ONLY RESIDUE REMAINING ON THE INNER BOAT SURFACES. THE BOAT WAS CAREFULLY FOLDED TO AVOID MORE SPILLAGE AND THEN TRANSFERRED TO A GARAGE AND LEFT TO AIR OUT.

Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: OIL, FUEL: NO. 2
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: O.S.I.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 350 gallons
CALLER STATED AS HE WAS WALKING HIS DOG WHEN HE SMELLED OIL, AT THE SAME TIME A RESIDENT CAME OUT OF A HOUSE WITH OIL UP TO HIS KNEES SCREAMING AT THE DRIVER OF THE OIL TRUCK. APPRENTLY THE DRIVER DELIVERED OIL TO THE WRONG ADDRESS. THE HOME HE DELIVERED TO HAS AN OIL RECEPTICAL ON THE OUTSIDE BUT THE STORAGE TANK HAS BEEN REMOVED. THE OIL WAS PUMP INTO THE BASEMENT OF A HOME WITHOUT A TANK TO STORE THE OIL SO THE OIL SPILLED ON TO A CONCRET FLOOR. AS STATED THIS IS THE WRONG ADDRESS FOR THE OIL DELIVERY. AN INSURANCE ADJUSTER FOR THE HOME OWNER DID ARRIVE ON THE SCENE. AT THIS TIME THE DRIVER DROPPED HIS BOOK AND RAN OFF DOWN THE STREET AND LEFT HIS TRUCK IN THE STREET.

Report Description/// POTENTIAL RELEASE /// THE CALLER REPORTED A FISHING VESSEL IS AGROUND AND ON FIRE ON A SAND BAR AND POTENTIALLY RELEASING GASOLINE ON MARCO ISLAND AT THE INCIDENT LOCATION. THE CALLER STATED THERE IS APPROXIMATELY 200 GALLONS OF GASOLINE ONBOARD. THE CALLER STATED THE SRP RAN INTO A RIVER MILE MARKER, AND WAS APPROACHED BY SEATOW WHO WITNESSED THE COLLISION. AFTER SEATOW APPROACHED THE FISHING VESSEL IT APPEARED THAT THE SRP WAS INTOXICATED AND ENDED UP SHOOTING FLARES INTO THE FISHING VESSEL THAT CAUGHT ON FIRE. THE SRP EVENTUALLY STOLE SEATOW'S VESSEL BY PUSHING THE SEATOW CAPTAIN OFF OF THE VESSEL AND HEADING SOUTH DOWN THE WATERWAY. THE SRP WAS APPREHENDED BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES A SHORT TIME LATER HIDING IN THE WOODS.

CONFIDENCE WAS DETERMINED TO BE MEDIUM-HIGH GIVEN THAT NO SPECIFIC POINT SOURCE COULD BE IDENTIFIED, AND NO OIL SLICKS WERE REPORTED IN THE AREA. Nearest City: Winnie, TX
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: BURNING INSULATION FROM FIRE
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: CTL TRANSPORTATION, LLC
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 3 gallons
DRIVER WAS WEST BOUND ON INTERSTATE 10 NEAR WINNIE TEXAS WHEN HE NOTICED SMOKE COMING FROM THE CENTER OF THE TRAILER. HE STOPPED AT MILE MARKER 822 TO SEE WHAT WAS SMOKING. WINDS WERE FROM SE AT ABOUT 8 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: NONE.

Nearest City: Cheyenne, WY
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: SUFURIC ACID
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: FRONTIER REFINING INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 600 gallons
THERE WAS A SPILL OF AN ESTIMATED VOLUME OF 600-700 GALLONS OF SULFURIC ACID FROM A LINE BREAK ON A STORAGE TANK. THE TANK IS NEXT TO ONE OF THE COOLING TOWERS. ICE THAT ACCUMULATED ON THE SIDES OF THE TOWERS DUE TO THE COLD WEATHER FELL AND BROKE A LINE CONNECTED TO THE TANK. THE TANK WAS FILLED EARLY LAST WEEK WITH 700-GALLONS. WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR CHEMICAL EXPOSURE AROUND THE TANK, A TRUE GAUGE HAS NOT BEEN TAKEN. INITIAL VOLUME ESTIMATES OVER THE WEEKEND WERE LOW (BELOW THE RQ). THE RELEASE IS CONTAINED AND THE SOIL IS BEING NEUTRALIZED WITH SODA ASH.

Nearest City: St. Louis, MO

Material: 32% UREA, AMMONIUM NITRATE SOLUTION
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: BRIMSTONE TOW
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 38.695459, -90.218914 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 50 gallons
Report Description
THERE WAS A RELEASE OF APROXIMATELY 50 GALLONS OF 32% UREA AMMONIUM NITRATE SOLUTION DURING THE BARGE (MM109) TO STORAGE TANK TRANSFER. THIS OCCURED AROUND 4:00 A.M. ON OCTOBER 27TH. THE TRANSFER PIPE WAS OVER STRETCHED AND BURST. THE VALVES WERE CLOSED AND THE TRANSFER PIPE WAS REPLACED. THE USCG RESPONDED TO THE GROUNDED BARGES AND INSPECTED MM109 AND MT1107. THE TOW WAS DELIVERED TO THIS DOCK BY THE "BRIMSTONE". USCG BOARDED THE TOW AROUND 0930 AND REMAINED ABOARD TO OBSERVE FURTHER ACTIONS.

REPORT DATE: 08-19-2021 REPORT TIME: 0130 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: GRAND ISLE 25 IMAGE DATE: 08-18-2021 IMAGE TIME: 1632 UTC DATA SOURCE: LANDSAT8 MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 30 METER LOCATION: 29°06"22" N/90°05"16" W AREA: 3.13 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THE POTENTIAL POINT SOURCE COULD HAVE BEEN A PIPELINE THAT INTERSECTED WITH THE ANOMALY. THE ANOMALY IS BELIEVED TO BE RELATED TO NRC# 1314105. THE ANOMALY MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 5.95 NMI LONG AND HAD A WIDTH OF ROUGHLY 0.23 NMI WIDE. WINDS AROUND THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE 5 KTS COMING FROM THE SW. UNCERTAINTIES: THE ANALYZED EXTENT OF THE ANOMALY IS APPROXIMATE DUE TO THE POSSIBILITY THAT CLOUDS WERE PARTIALLY COVERING THE ANOMALY.

CALLER STATED THIS MORNING 13-JAN-2010 AT THE PORT OF GULFPORT A RADIATION HIT ON A CONTAINER WAS DISCOVERED . THE CUSTOMS BOARDER PROTECTION PERSONNEL CHECKED OUT THE CONTAINER AND THE PORT WAS SHUT DOWN AT 0755 HOURS UNTIL 0845 HOURS. THE CONTAINER IN QUESTION CONTAINED SILICON SAND WHICH GAVE A FALSE READING OF RADIATION. CALLER STATED THERE WAS NO REAL HAZARD TO THE CARGO . CALLER STATED THERE WAS NO EVACUATION JUST A SHUTDOWN FOR FIFTY MINUTES UNTIL THE CONTAINER WAS CHECKED OUT BY CUSTOMS BOARDER PROTECTION AT THAT POINT THE GATES WERE REOPENED. properties.title: NRC Report: Toluene in Storm Drain near Los Angeles, CA
properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 968548 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: THE BLAKELY PAINTING CO.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 968548
Incident Time: 2011-02-22 16:00:00
Nearest City: Los Angeles, CA
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: TOLUENE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: THE BLAKELY PAINTING CO.
Skytruth Analysis
DURING A PHASE I DUE DILIGENCE INSPECTION OF THE NEIGHBORING BUSINESS, AN REA OBSERVED PILES OF USED PAINT CANS, F-TYPE CHEMICAL BOTTLES, 5 GALLON BUCKETS, TRASH CANS, SPRAY CANS, USED PAINT ROLLERS, QUART PAINT CANS, TRASH, AND DEBRIS STOCK PILED ALONG THE SOUTHERN PORTION OF THE PARCEL IDENTIFIED AS 5220-025-034 (EAST OF 5537 ALHAMBRA AVENUE). LIQUIDS RELEASED FROM THIS STOCK PILE OF HAZARDOUS CHEMICAL CONTAINERS WAS OBSERVED LEAVING THE SUBJECT PROPERTY UNDER A FENCE ALONG THE SOUTHERN PORTION OF THE SITE. THESE CHEMICALS AND LIQUIDS WERE OBSERVED LEAKING IN A SOUTHERLY DIRECTION DOWN A DRIVEWAY INTO TWO STORM WATER DRAINS WHICH FLOW TO THE OCEAN. STAINING IS OBSERVED ALONG THE WALKWAYS INDICATING FORMER RELEASES INTO THE STORMWATER DRAINS. IT IS ASSUMED THAT THE CHEMICAL CONTAINERS AND ODORS AT THE SITE INDICATE THE MATERIALS BEING RELEASED INTO THE STORMWATER DRAINS ARE IN FACT CHEMICALS USED AT THAT SITE AND STOCKPILED ALONG THE SOUTHERN PROPERTY LINE. STAINING AND ODORS ALSO INDICATE THAT THE MATERIALS RELEASED INTO THE DRAINS ARE NOT WATER SOLUBLE AND CONTAIN TOLUENE DUE TO THE ODORS AT THE SITE.

Lat/Long: 28.298836, -81.405583 (Approximated from route)
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** A 24' BAYLINER VESSEL SANK AT THE EAST LAKE FISH CAMP IN KISSIMMEE, FLORIDA ON THURSDAY JUNE 6, 2013. THE SWO WAS NOTIFIED AND SUBSEQUENTLY NOTIFIED ORLANDO OER ON SATURDAY, JUNE 8, 2013. AT THAT TIME IT WAS REPORTED THAT THE VESSEL HAD BEEN SHEENING BUT WAS NO LONGER SHEENING. EFFORTS WERE BEING MADE BY LOCAL LE TO LOCATE THE OWNER OF THE VESSEL. THESE EFFORTS HAVE BEEN UNSUCCESSFUL. THE STAFF AT THE FISH CAMP HAVE PLACED SKIRTED BOOM AROUND THE VESSEL AND ARE ATTEMPTING TO FLOAT THE VESSEL FOR REMOVAL. A LIGHT SHEEN HAS BEEN OBSERVED BUT IT IS CONTAINED WITHIN SKIRTED BOOM WITH SORBENTS PLACED WITHIN. SWO INCIDENT NUMBER 2013-3601. THIS REPORT IS BEING MADE FOR NOTIFICATION TO EPA DUTY OFFICER IN THE EVENT THAT FISH CAMP STAFF UNSUCCESSFUL IN FLOATING VESSEL AND FURTHER ACTION REQUIRED TO ABATE FUEL/OIL RELEASE THREAT. MARINA IS LOCATED ON EAST LAKE TOHOPEKALIGA, INLAND WATERWAY.
